target_customer: Film and TV production teams, mainly assistant directors and unit production managers who build production schedules
problem: Production scheduling in film and TV relied on legacy desktop tools like Movie Magic Scheduling that were hard to share and collaborate on.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription per production or seat (pricing not verified)
product_category: film and TV production scheduling software

founders.name: Herman Phillips
prior_employers: Productions in assistant directors department including The Mandalorian, Silicon Valley, Euphoria, Insecure, The Fabelmans
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Assistant Directors department credits; no education listed.

founders.name: Roger Tran
founders.background_notes: YC page lists UX, architecture, real estate development and location rentals; mentions Stanford and Harvard without degrees.

competitors.name: Movie Magic Scheduling
competitors.what: Legacy desktop production scheduling software from Entertainment Partners, the incumbent standard

competitors.name: StudioBinder
competitors.what: Web based production management and scheduling suite

technical_complexity.rationale: Collaborative scheduling app with real-time sync and script import; standard SaaS engineering with some domain complexity for episodic and multi-unit logic.

defensibility.rationale: Incumbent Movie Magic had habit lock-in, but a new tool had to win each production; integrations with call sheet and budgeting tools add modest stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wrapbook, a production payroll platform, acquired Cinapse in December 2025 per an acquisition tracker and the company site, which now calls itself a Wrapbook company.

market_need_then: Schedulers and ADs worked in a decades old desktop tool where collaboration meant file passing; the company's pitch rests on that gap, and a 2024 product launch followed.

identity.visual_style: Clean, industry focused, studio logos and testimonials
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and direct, insider friendly: Built by filmmakers, for filmmakers

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself; credibility came from AD testimonials rather than name recognition.

outcome_analysis: Cinapse was a two person team led by a working assistant director who targeted the scheduling tool at the heart of Hollywood production. It launched to users in February 2024 and, per an acquisition tracker and its own site, was acquired by Wrapbook in December 2025 for an undisclosed price. Funding detail is thin, so the outcome looks like a small, domain led exit.
notes: Directory status says Active but sources indicate acquisition by Wrapbook in 2025-12 (aggregator plus company site calling itself a Wrapbook company). Funding: CB Insights aggregator lists about $770K over 6 rounds and a 2022 seed, a Wefunder page and a pre-seed claim exist; all unverified from one aggregator so not recorded as rounds. Competitors named on Cinapse site and 2025 profile, not dated near the 2022 batch; Movie Magic and StudioBinder pre-existed the batch. Signal Base lists Cinapse in Belgium, likely an error. Recorded rounds rest on single databases (FundedIQ pre-seed 100K Dec 2021; CB Insights seed 2022 and a convertible note of 2024-11-22, no amounts). CB Insights total is 770K over 6 rounds with investors Wefunder, Gaingels, Unpopular Ventures and Y Combinator; Crowdability claims about 2.5M; another aggregator says 125K in Jan 2022. Totals conflict and remain unresolved. Acquisition by Wrapbook announced 2025-12-08 (PR Newswire), terms undisclosed.
